caption: The drawing depicts a set of double wooden doors set within an arched doorway. The wooden doors are vertically aligned, each adorned with irregular, wavy lines. Surrounding the doors is a brick arch, with red and brown hues, forming a complete semicircle above the doorway. The brickwork continues as a border down both sides and forms a rectangular base on each side of the doorway. The door is set into a cream-colored or light beige wall, with subtle shading and sparse, sketch-like indications of texture and brickwork. Above the arch, there is a feature with a blue cross set into a rounded niche outlined in red. Below the doors is a floor area composed of rectangular tiles in shades of brown, red, and beige. The drawing contains a label reading “Main doors,” as well as a four-foot scale bar and the name “Geoffrey Holt” signed at the bottom right.
title: Doorway, Main Entrance to Mission
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
